name: Low Carb Taco Cabbage Beef Skillet
writer_notes: SOURCE YIELD 3, rebuilt to 14 at the mapper's 4.6667x scale. Every gram and buy string transcribed from mapped\low-carb-taco-cabbage-beef-skillet.json; no number computed in prose.

MACROS transcribed from the build's own food-macros-db recompute at 14 servings: 532 cal, 33 g protein, about 8.5 g carbs, 39 g fat per serving. In band for this run (400 to 650 cal, 35 g carb or less). None of these are the source card's numbers; the source published 576 cal / 50 g protein, and the mapper flagged that 50 g protein is arithmetically impossible for the source's own ingredient list (ceiling 38.2 g), a source-side raw/cooked double-count. Our figures are the defensible recompute.

BEEF FAT CLASS is load-bearing on the floor, per the mapper's ruled_substitutions. The mapper booked 80/20 (the source's own published 37 g fat reproduces at 80/20, ours 38.6, and would collapse to about 19 g at 93/7). At 80/20 the dish computes 532 cal PASS; the house 93/7 row would compute about 368 cal and FAIL the 400 floor. If the house later prefers lean beef here the recipe cannot pass the band as a 3-serving-per-pound dish and must be re-based or dropped, not fudged.

EVERY BOUGHT INGREDIENT IS USED BY A STEP and no step uses anything unbought. Walked the costed list against the steps both directions: ground beef (steps 3, 4), salsa (4), chili powder (4), green cabbage (2, 4, 5), Mexican cheese blend (6). Salt and pepper are the source's to-taste line, mapped optional-pantry at zero grams and NOT booked as a cost line, so no step names them; step 5 says 'season to taste' only. The source's optional garnishes (sour cream, green onions, avocado) are mapped optional-unquantified at zero grams and NOT bought, so no step calls for them and prose does not stage them as included; the intro notes toppings are the cook's own add-on.

SHOP_SMART makes NO leftover, per-ounce, or lasts-several-batches claim, so no bullet requires a cost_lines entry to prove it; every statement is grounded in the recipe's own buy amount. Re-walk the bullets against cost_lines once costed before publish.

BLOCKER FLAG for the repair pass: '80/20 Ground Beef' has NO row in db\ingredients.json (the price map), though the mapper cites board bid ground-beef-8020 with full cells across 7 of 7 stores and the public feed carries ground-beef-8020. As shipped this build prices the beef unwired/pantry-static, so the cost_ps is a FLOOR until the item is wired. This is the same unwired-item pattern the stroganoff intake documented, and it is shared with keto-cheeseburger-skillet in this run, which also books '80/20 Ground Beef'. The writer does not touch db\ingredients.json; wiring the item to bid ground-beef-8020 (gpu 453.592, unit lb) belongs to the repair pass before the audit gate.
intro_html: Taco night is one of the cheapest ways to feed a crowd, right up until the shells, the tortillas, and the seasoning packets pile the carbs and the cost back on. This one keeps the taco and throws out the wrapper. You brown the beef, stir in salsa and chili powder for the whole taco flavor with no packet, then wilt shredded cabbage down in the pan where the shells used to be and melt cheese over the top. It eats like a taco bowl you can portion into containers. Built at 14 servings it runs about {{cal}} calories and {{protein}} grams of protein a serving, with under 10 grams of carbs. Top your bowl with whatever you like when you eat it; the build is just the skillet. That is taco night that does not fight your macros or your wallet.
ingredients_display: Mexican Cheese Blend (Great Value): 3 1/2 cups shredded (396 g)
cost_note_html: Real Omaha store prices from our weekly grocery board (2026). They still swing by store and by what is on sale.
cost_lines: Green Cabbage, 9 1/3 cups shredded (about 3/4 head): ~$1.22. Buy 1 head: $1.69.
Mexican Cheese Blend, 3 1/2 cups shredded: ~$3.01. Buy 2 8 oz bags: $3.45.
Pantry seasonings (chili powder): ~$0.30. From jars you keep on hand.

Batch total: about $30.44 across 14 servings, so roughly $2.17 per bowl. This counts only the amounts this batch actually uses from each package, so it is the cost of the food in the containers, not a register receipt.

True shopping cost: about $34.09 across 14 servings, roughly $2.44 per bowl. What the register trip looks like if your pantry is already stocked. Meat, produce, and packaged items are counted as the whole packages you have to buy, since you cannot grab a partial box, can, or jar. Pantry staples you already own (rice, seasonings, oils, and long-lasting sauces) are counted at only what this batch uses.

Starting with an empty pantry? Add about $0.60 one time. That is the extra cost of buying full containers of every pantry staple in this recipe instead of just the amounts used, which puts a first shopping trip near $34.69. Those containers then feed this batch and many more after it.
cost_closing_html: About ${{cost_ps}} a serving (at everyday cost) for a taco bowl you eat with a fork. The beef carries it and the cheese finishes it; the salsa, chili powder, and cabbage turn a pound of ground beef into a full skillet for almost nothing.
shop_smart: Nearly five pounds of ground beef is the anchor. Reach for the 80/20 so the skillet tastes like a real taco instead of dry crumbles, and buy the big family pack instead of the little trays so you are paying for beef, not packaging. This is where most of the money and most of the protein live.

Cabbage is what the shells used to be. You want about three quarters of a head of green cabbage shredded, which cooks down soft in the pan and bulks the whole skillet out for almost nothing. It is the cheapest thing in the cart and it is what makes a pound of beef feed this many people without carbs.

Salsa and chili powder are the entire taco seasoning. A jar of salsa and a few tablespoons of chili powder from the spice rack do the job a whole rack of seasoning packets charges you for, with no cornstarch or sugar filler riding along. That is the whole flavor of the dish for pocket change.

Shredded Mexican blend melts it all together. Three and a half cups of full-fat Mexican cheese blend stirred in off the heat pulls the skillet into something that eats like a loaded taco. Buy the real full-fat bag rather than the low-fat kind, because the fat is what melts smooth instead of turning rubbery.
make_it: Weigh your empty skillet or the biggest pot you own and write the number down. You will use it at the end to split this into 14 even servings by weight instead of eyeballing every container.
Shred the cabbage into thin strips if it did not come pre-shredded.
Set a large skillet over medium heat and brown the ground beef, breaking it into small pieces until it is cooked through, then drain off the fat.
Add the salsa, chili powder, and shredded cabbage to the pan and bring it up to a low boil.
Cover, reduce the heat to medium, and cook for 10 to 12 minutes until the cabbage is soft, then season to taste.
Turn off the heat and stir in the shredded cheese until it melts through.
Weigh the full pot, subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1, divide by 14, and spoon that exact weight into each container.
portion_html: Set the full pot on your scale and subtract the empty weight you wrote down in Step 1 to get the cooked total. Divide that number by 14 and spoon that exact weight into each container. Every serving lands near {{cal}} calories with {{protein}} grams of protein.
